archetypes.name: routing-surface-audit
archetypes.rationale: The plan retargets Step 3b→Step 4 routing across four named surfaces but may miss routing prose in sketch-launch.md or caller-doc files that could allow bypassing the new completion boundary.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each scope file, identify every prose line, comment, and blockquote that names a routing transition from Step 3b to Step 4 — via arrow, comma, slash, or routing verb (continue, proceed, route, jump, enter, go). Cross-reference against the four scan surfaces the plan names: Step 3b slice, Gate-B-bypass slice in SKILL.md, approval-gates.md, and run-step3-review.sh. Flag any additional files or regions containing Step 3b→Step 4 routing prose that the plan does not include in its retarget inventory. Verify that sketch-launch.md, design-driver.md, and finalize-plan.md contain no routing prose that would allow a reader or orchestrator to reach Step 4 while bypassing the completion boundary. Check whether the harness routing-guard patterns described in the plan (the named verb set plus arrow/comma/slash shorthands) cover all routing forms actually present across the scope files. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: guard-logic
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces two conditional guards (SIMPLE branch in Step 2a, .completed/finalize absence in Step 4) that must compose correctly; gaps or overlaps in session state coverage could silently skip or double-run artifact creation.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the plan's specification of the Step 2a entry-fence SIMPLE guard and the Step 4 entry-fence compatibility guard, checking that the described logic is complete and non-overlapping across all observable session states — every combination of .completed/step-2a, .completed/step-2a.5, .completed/step-3b, and .completed/finalize present or absent. Verify the plan explicitly prevents HARD paths from entering the SIMPLE sentinel branch and that all three sentinel writes plus both .completed marker writes are inside the guarded branch only, never unconditional. Identify any run state where neither guard fires but artifacts are still expected, or where both guards could fire and produce a double-write. Check whether the Step 4 compatibility guard is specified as an inner addition to the existing timing fence rather than a replacement fence, and whether the plan's test-design-structure.sh assertion changes correctly scope positive pins to the guarded branch rather than asserting bare unconditional literals. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
